newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ mid-dated and long bond yields close lower.
newsitem.headline: NZ mid-dated and long bond yields close lower.

text.p: New Zealand mid-dated and long bond yields pushed lower on Thursday while bank bills nudged down just a couple of points.
"The market has the warm fuzzies. I'm not sure why. It was an outstanding performance," said a Wellington bond dealer.
The 2/01 bond yields closed eight basis points lower while the 10 year bonds closed five points lower.

There were a number of news items which gave a mixed picture for the inflation outlook -- slightly higher unemployment, strong building consents data for July, and marginally lower house prices but higher sales turnover.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank's could not take any comfort from data of clear evidence of inflation pressures easing.
Bill traders are becoming wary of the bank as the 90-day bills neared 9.75 percent.

"There are a few out there in the camp, where if the Trade-Weighted Index and the currency continue to go up then the Reserve Bank may be forced to say something. But I myself think they will be reluctant to say something ahead of the election," said an Auckland dealer. He said it would take a sustained period of the TWI at a 75-100 basis point higher level for the bank to be too concerned.
The October 12 election remains firmly in the background but a poll due in the National Business Review on Friday morning may stimulate fresh interest.
Dealers said the market is flow driven and the flows, backed by euro and dual currency samurai issues, were positive at present.
